command: grok --permission-mode default (interactive TUI, driven under a pty)
note: The gate arrives as a notification envelope with notificationType `permission_prompt` (the idle one that follows is `idle_prompt`) — grok registers Notification and PermissionDenied, so this wiring was already right. The transcript is `updates.jsonl`: grok writes five jsonl siblings per session and the one-line rewind_points.jsonl is the newest, which is why the harvest now asks corpus_check --list instead of the filesystem. Home path redacted to /Users/dev.
